differences.what: Write-up credits a second origin for the method's mechanism (the j-lens-mean project's counterfactual idea), which the message omits entirely
differences.message_quote: This is the white-bear direction from Raman et al. (2026), which I attribute honestly.
differences.writeup_quote: This is also the counterfactual idea the j-lens-mean project documents — that the plain J-lens fails because it reads `J_l h` around an off-manifold zero, and the fix is a matched counterfactual — but realised as a *direction* rather than a subtracted mean.

message_source_quote: This is the white-bear direction from Raman et al. (2026), which I attribute honestly.
writeup_source_quote: The contrast is Raman, Wierzbicki & Fournier's "white-bear" notion (2026): the model represents its *stance toward* a concept separately from the concept, and pushing it toward "holding it in mind while doing something else" makes the layers above the band keep developing the implied concept instead of dropping it for next-token prediction.
rationale: Both documents explicitly credit Raman et al. (2026)'s white-bear stance notion as the basis of the hold/suppress contrast, and both frame the novelty as mapping the broader contrast space (testing many content/format alternatives) with the stance direction as the sole survivor. The message adds an unverified quoted attribution to the source paper ('we did not try content contrasts') not present in the write-up, and omits the write-up's secondary attribution to the j-lens-mean project's counterfactual idea as co-origin of the mechanism.
